evals.name: choose-watcher-mode-and-json-path
evals.prompt: I opened PR #412 on this repo and want you to babysit it in a standard command-execution harness that only returns command output after a process exits. Which gh_pr_watch.py flag should you loop on, why shouldn't you use --watch or --snapshot for the main wait, and where do you read the recommended actions in each mode (including --retry-failed-now)?
assertions: Selects --once (default blocking poll) as the main loop mode for harnesses that return output only on command exit
Explains that --watch streams JSONL events for harnesses reading live output and --snapshot returns immediately without waiting
Reads top-level actions for --once and --snapshot
Reads snapshot.actions (with top-level rerun_attempted, rerun_count, reason) for --retry-failed-now
Reads payload.snapshot.actions on snapshot events and payload.actions on stop events for --watch

evals.name: retry-flaky-e2e-vs-diagnose-unit-failure
evals.prompt: gh_pr_watch.py --pr 412 --once just returned failed_runs showing two failures on head abc1234: `e2e-desktop` (retry_eligible: true, timed out talking to staging) and `jvm-unit-tests` (retry_eligible: false, compile error in a file my PR touched). Should I run --retry-failed-now right away?
assertions: Says NOT to run --retry-failed-now while a non-retryable branch-caused failure exists
Diagnoses jvm-unit-tests as branch-caused and starts fixing it locally rather than rerunning CI
Notes that --retry-failed-now only reruns workflows matching retry_eligible_workflow_keywords when all failures are retry-eligible and checks are terminal
Mentions the per-head-SHA retry budget (3 by default, surfacing stop_exhausted_retries when exhausted) and that pushing a fix commit resets the head SHA

evals.name: codex-eyes-reaction-and-idle-wait-expired
evals.prompt: How does babysit-pr track Codex reviews when Codex has no GitHub check run? Specifically: what happens right after a push when there is no 👀 reaction yet, what should I do if gh_pr_watch.py returns request_codex_review vs stop_ready_to_merge with codex_gate.idle_wait_expired: true, and do I need to resolve Codex's `Didn't find any major issues` comment?
assertions: Explains that chatgpt-codex-connector[bot] signals an active review via a 👀 reaction on the PR plus the Codex Review Summary comment for the current head SHA
States that an absent 👀 reaction right after push is not enough when Codex is active on the PR — the watcher waits for a Completed review of head_sha or idle_wait_minutes
Comments `@codex review` on the PR when request_codex_review (or a failed review under diagnose_codex_review) is returned
Tells the PR owner that Codex did not review the current head (surfacing codex_gate.note) when stop_ready_to_merge arrives with codex_gate.idle_wait_expired: true
Treats Codex's `Didn't find any major issues` comment and summary table as status/clean completion rather than actionable review items

evals.name: pr-af-advisory-check-blocking-comments
evals.prompt: Our repo has pr_af.enabled set to true with label `pr-af`. On PR #518 the `PR-AF Review` GitHub Actions job failed with exit code 1, and `github-actions[bot]` also posted an inline comment containing the configured pr_af.review_body_markers text. Does the failed PR-AF check block merge, does the comment block merge, and should I add `github-actions` to review_bot_login_keywords?
assertions: Explains that the PR-AF check itself is advisory: while running (or within missing_check_grace_minutes) it holds readiness with wait_pr_af, but a failed, skipped, cancelled, or hung PR-AF check never counts as a CI failure
States that marked PR-AF review comments ARE blocking review items that must be triaged and resolved before merge
Explicitly warns NEVER to add the shared github-actions[bot] login to review_bot_login_keywords

evals.name: push-once-batching-with-local-gate
evals.prompt: While babysitting PR #601, the `lint` workflow failed on a formatting violation I introduced, `unit-tests` is still running, and Codex still has its 👀 reaction on the PR. I already fixed the lint issue in 30 seconds. Should I commit and push right now so CI restarts faster?
assertions: Says NOT to push yet because every push restarts CI and triggers a new round of bot reviews
Approves fixing the branch-caused failure locally right away without waiting idle
Requires waiting until running checks and review bots (including Codex's 👀 review) finish so any additional findings fold into the same batch
Requires running the configured local_gate (or repo check command when local_gate is null) green before pushing once

evals.name: triage-2x2-matrix-and-loop-breakers
evals.prompt: Rounds 1 and 2 of bot reviews on my small null-handling fix PR only had minor style suggestions (no blockers). Now on round 3, a bot flagged two items: (1) a real pre-existing race condition in an untouched class on main that would cause data loss under load, and (2) another round of stricter input validation on a helper I only added in round 1 and already tweaked in round 2 for that same bot. How should I triage both findings, and should I keep going for round 4?
assertions: Applies the 2x2 triage matrix (In scope vs Out of scope x Blocker vs Improvement) and names the box in the reply
Classifies (1) as Out of scope + Blocker because the defect already exists on the base branch without this PR, filing an issue and linking it on the PR rather than expanding scope
Recognizes (2) as an Improvement and triggers the loop-breaker rule (three rounds without an in-scope blocker, or twice in a row on code added only for an earlier finding)
Stops and asks the owner with concrete diff stats (commits, files, lines), saving any out-of-scope work on a followup/<topic> branch before reverting

evals.name: inline-reply-and-graphql-thread-resolution
evals.prompt: gh_pr_watch.py shows `blocking_review_items` has two unresolved inline threads: one from `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]` (comment id 1987654321) that is out of scope so I filed issue #902 and made no code change, and one open inline note I posted myself earlier. Give me the exact steps and gh API calls so blocking_review_items clears.
assertions: Explains that blocking_review_items blocks readiness until empty, including open inline threads started by the authenticated account

Replies in-thread using REST POST repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/<pr>/comments/<comment-id>/replies (not gh pr comment, which posts a top-level PR comment) with the triage rationale and issue link before resolving an unchanged bot finding
Queries reviewThreads via GraphQL to find the thread node IDs (PRRT_...) and resolves both threads via the GraphQL resolveReviewThread mutation

evals.name: update-behind-or-conflicting-branch-via-merge
evals.prompt: gh_pr_watch.py returned `diagnose_branch_behind` on PR #710, which comes from a contributor fork targeting upstream's `release/2.4` branch. Should I run `git fetch origin main && git rebase origin/main && git push --force`?
assertions: Rejects assuming `main`, using `origin` blindly on a fork, rebasing unasked, and using plain `git push --force`
Checks the actual base branch via `gh pr view <n> --json baseRefName` (`release/2.4`) and fetches from the target upstream repository remote rather than the fork's `origin`
Merges the updated base branch into the PR branch (preserving history so a normal push suffices) unless the owner explicitly asked to rebase (which would use --force-with-lease)
Verifies no review bot is running, runs local_gate, verifies earlier fixes remain intact, and pushes once

evals.name: stop-ready-to-merge-sole-authority
evals.prompt: gh_pr_watch.py exited with an error because .agents/skills/babysit-pr/config.json had a string instead of a list for required_checks, so I ran `gh pr checks 77` directly — it printed `no checks reported`, and `gh pr view 77` shows `MERGEABLE`. Can I tell the user PR #77 is green and merge it now?
assertions: Refuses to declare the PR ready or merge based on raw `gh pr checks` or `gh pr view` output

States that gh_pr_watch.py (`stop_ready_to_merge`) is the sole authority on merge readiness and a broken watcher/config must be reported or fixed as a tooling/config error rather than bypassed with ad-hoc polling
Points out that zero checks (`no checks reported` / `check_count == 0`) is NEVER ready and maps to `diagnose_no_checks`

evals.name: post-merge-cleanup-merged-vs-closed
evals.prompt: gh_pr_watch.py just exited with `stop_pr_closed` for PR #815 (`feature/cache` checked out in `.worktrees/feature-cache`), and config.json has `cleanup.branch_delete_requires_approval: true`. Walk me through the exact checks and cleanup commands I must run — both if it was closed unmerged and if it was squash-merged.
assertions: Checks `pr.merged` in the snapshot or `gh pr view 815 --json mergedAt` first: if closed without merging, keeps the worktree and branch untouched and reports to the owner
Runs all cleanup commands from the main checkout (never from inside `.worktrees/feature-cache`) and never deletes remote branches
Removes the linked worktree first via `git worktree remove` without `--force` (stopping if dirty)
Asks the owner for approval before deleting the local branch because `cleanup.branch_delete_requires_approval` is `true`
Verifies `git rev-parse feature/cache` equals the merged PR's `headRefOid` before running `git branch -D feature/cache`, then runs `git pull --ff-only` on the base branch

evals.name: diagnose-merge-blocked-and-missing-required-checks
evals.prompt: All reported checks on PR #880 passed, there are no unresolved threads or conflicts, yet gh_pr_watch.py returned `diagnose_merge_blocked`. On another PR #881 it returned `diagnose_missing_required_checks` with `checks.required_missing: ["check"]`. How do I handle each?
assertions: For `diagnose_merge_blocked`, inspects branch protection / rulesets via `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/<base>` for required code-owner reviews, required commit signatures, or unreported status checks, reports the blocker to the owner, and never bypasses it

For `diagnose_missing_required_checks`, investigates why the check in `checks.required_missing` did not run (such as path/branch filters, disabled workflows, or non-PR triggers) and reports findings to the owner

evals.name: preflight-wrong-checkout-and-dirty-worktree
evals.prompt: You were asked to babysit PR #905 (`fix/auth-timeout`, head SHA `9f8e7d6`). You run a snapshot and find a branch-caused test failure to fix, but your current shell is on `main` with uncommitted edits in two unrelated files. What do you do before touching any code?
assertions: Catches the preflight invariant that `HEAD` must match the PR's `head_branch` (`fix/auth-timeout`) at `head_sha` (`9f8e7d6`) before editing
Does NOT edit on `main` and does NOT stash/reset/overwrite the unrelated uncommitted changes
Checks out the PR branch in its own isolated git worktree (or stops and asks the owner when unrelated uncommitted changes make safe work uncertain)

evals.name: gitlab-mr-green-and-manual-job
evals.prompt: Babysit https://gitlab.example.com/platform/api/-/merge_requests/58 on our self-hosted GitLab. glab_mr_watch.py --once first returned diagnose_skipping_checks naming the job `deploy_review_app` (manual, allow_failure false); after the owner clicked Run and the pipeline went green it returned stop_ready_to_merge with pr.detailed_merge_status `mergeable`. Which script and preflight do you use, what do you do on each result, and can `glab ci view` showing a green pipeline replace the watcher?
assertions: Uses scripts/glab_mr_watch.py (not gh_pr_watch.py) and preflights with `glab auth status --hostname gitlab.example.com`
On diagnose_skipping_checks, tells the owner the blocking manual job needs someone to click Run and does not play it (or any deploy job) without the owner's go-ahead
Treats stop_ready_to_merge from the watcher as the only green signal; glab ci view / glab mr view are for diagnosis only
Follows repo rules on merging instead of merging on its own

evals.name: gitlab-need-rebase-merge-not-rebase
evals.prompt: glab_mr_watch.py returned diagnose_branch_behind for MR !58 (`feature/rate-limits` into `develop`) with pr.detailed_merge_status `need_rebase`. GitLab shows a Rebase button and a teammate also pushes to this branch. How do you update the branch?
assertions: Reads the real target branch (`develop`, from pr.base_branch) rather than assuming main
Merges the target into the MR branch locally, runs local_gate, and pushes once
Does NOT use GitLab's Rebase button, the /rebase quick action, or a plain force-push on the shared branch

evals.name: watch-in-a-cheap-subagent-no-hand-written-polling
evals.prompt: You are babysitting PR #930 in a harness that can spawn subagents. Where should the blocking `--once` wait run, what exactly should the subagent return, and what happens between cycles? If the watcher does not cover a state, may the main agent write its own `gh pr checks` polling loop?
assertions: Runs every wait (`--once` or `--watch`) in a subagent at the lowest model tier and lowest reasoning effort, with no file edits, pushes, or diagnosis
The subagent returns one action line plus only the identifiers the main agent needs, never the full snapshot JSON, comment bodies, or logs
The main agent acts on that line and starts a new subagent for the next cycle
Without subagents, runs `--once` in the main agent and keeps only the action line
Never writes a hand-written polling loop in the main agent; a state the watcher does not cover is reported as a tooling gap

evals.name: post-merge-pipeline-success-and-failure
evals.prompt: PR #940 was squash-merged, and `stop_pr_closed` reported `pr.merged: true`. What should the same watch subagent run next, what does a successful result add to the stop line, and what do you do if it prints `failed: build`? Should you push a fix to the base branch or rerun the failed base-branch job?
assertions: Runs `--watch-merge-pipeline` in the same watch subagent after a merged `stop_pr_closed`; a closed unmerged PR skips it
Uses the base-branch merge commit (GitHub `mergeCommit.oid`), not the PR head SHA, and appends the bare result such as `merge_pipeline: success` to the action line
On `failed: <job>`, reports the job and pipeline URL to the owner and does not push to the base branch or rerun base-branch jobs unless the owner asks
Treats `canceled`, `manual: <job>`, `skipped`, `no_pipeline`, and `timeout` as report-only outcomes, not as failures to fix automatically
May proceed with normal post-merge cleanup after a successful pipeline

evals.name: gitlab-post-merge-squash-sha-and-manual-job
evals.prompt: On self-hosted GitLab, MR !72 was squash-merged into `develop`, and the project's `merge_method` is `ff`. Which SHA does `glab_mr_watch.py --watch-merge-pipeline` look up, how does it avoid a pipeline from another ref, and what should you do if it prints `no_pipeline` or `manual: deploy_prod`?
assertions: Uses `merge_commit_sha` first; on a fast-forward project falls back to `squash_commit_sha` for a squashed MR (the MR `sha` only when not squashed), and watches the actual target branch (`develop`)
Does not use `squash_commit_sha` as the target tip on a project whose `merge_method` is `merge` or `rebase_merge`; it waits for `merge_commit_sha` instead

Tracks every matching pipeline by SHA and target ref for the settle hold while the printed state comes from the newest pipeline; when the instance ignores ref, filters the SHA-only answer by the target branch
On `no_pipeline` after the 5-minute grace, reports a missing post-merge pipeline as a tooling gap instead of polling by hand
On `manual: deploy_prod`, tells the owner that a blocking manual job needs someone to click Run and never plays a deploy job without the owner's go-ahead
